title: "IV Encontro do PGMAT (2026)"
---

The **IV Encontro do PGMAT** is the annual meeting of the Graduate Program in Mathematics (PGMAT) at IGCE/UNESP, Rio Claro, where master's and doctoral students present their work in progress to the rest of the programme. It was held on 12–13 March 2026 at the Rio Claro campus.

This was my own master's programme, and I used the talk as a rehearsal for my dissertation defence: I presented an excerpt of the dissertation to an audience of colleagues and faculty from the programme.

## The work

**Aplicações do Teorema de Hahn-Banach à Teoria da Representação** — Marina Fuzaro Magossi, supervised by Profª Drª Suzete Maria Silva Afonso.

The talk follows a single thread: how far the two principles of the Hahn–Banach theorem — **extension** (a continuous linear functional on a subspace extends to the whole space, preserving the norm) and **separation** (two disjoint convex sets can be separated by a closed hyperplane) — carry the theory of integral representation in locally convex spaces.

The starting point is Carathéodory's theorem, which writes every point of a convex hull in $\mathbb{R}^n$ as a finite convex combination of at most $n+1$ extreme points — a discrete measure. In infinite dimension finite combinations are no longer enough, and the question becomes how to represent points of a compact convex set by a measure. The presentation then goes through Krein–Milman, Choquet's theorem, its Choquet–Bishop–de Leeuw extension to the non-metrisable case, the barycentre theorem, and Jensen's inequality, closing with a table that names the exact role Hahn–Banach plays in each of them.
